.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (verdicts, severity, known false positives incl. sign-in)
evidence: Built the criterion->requirement map for all 16 functional, 6 polish, 4 visual and 2 gate criteria. Almost every leg traces to the brief (walls/not-available: walls-and-retention.md:17; timers/holds/search/transcripts; conversations.md replies/edits/formatting/links/mentions/unread/live updates; integration.md clock/UTC/persistence). One instance grades an unrequired request shape/behaviour: tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:65-66 (wall_every_route leg 5) has Dev replay his recorded M-11 reply request with the parent swapped to M-13's 'Draft will sent for your review.' and demands 'it is refused too, and JUDGE-W3 appears in neither M-11 nor M-13', and line 66 fails 'if a refusal is anything but a plain not-available'. The brief only says 'A reply always belongs to the matter of the message it answers; nobody can reply from one matter to a message in another' (conversations.md:5) and 'Anyone who can see a matter can post and reply in it' (walls-and-retention.md:15); Dev can see M-13. The leg only works for the golden's shape POST /api/matters/:id/messages {parent_id} (server.js:395-410, app.js:482), and prompt.md itself says 'Any endpoint path, payload shape or cookie name is acceptable.' Second, smaller instance in the same leg: the plain not-available wording is required by the brief only for walled/non-own-matter access (walls-and-retention.md:17); for Dev's M-13-parent attempt (a matter he can see) a specific reason such as 'replies must stay in their parent's matter' is conforming and even favoured by walls-and-retention.md:37. Other legs checked and accepted: sign-out (professional default for a multi-account sign-in app; skill known FP), substring search 'urvey booked' (supported by 'exactly the characters typed', walls-and-retention.md:33), live cross-tab unread sync (conversations.md 'same in every tab' + ten-second live rule), placeholder/transcript/hold/timer legs, polish/visual legs. Source analysis only; no judge run exercises the counterexample.
counterexample: Conforming app whose reply request derives the matter from the parent, e.g. POST /api/messages/:parentId/replies (or POST /api/messages {matter_id, parent_id} where the server files the reply under the parent's matter). Replaying Dev's recorded reply with parent K-8 ('Draft will sent for your review.', M-13) creates a valid reply by Dev in M-13, a matter he can see, exactly as conversations.md:5 prescribes; nothing crosses matters. The judge sees a 201 and JUDGE-W3 in M-13, so wall_every_route (weight 4.0 of 42, binary) scores 0 although every wall route is airtight. Likewise a golden-shape app that refuses the M-13-parent replay with 'You can only reply within the same matter' fails the 'plain not-available' clause.
suggested_fix: In wall_every_route leg 5, accept either outcome for the M-13-parent replay: refused with any refusal, or filed as a reply in M-13 under 'Draft will sent for your review.'; the only failure is JUDGE-W3 appearing in M-11 (or as a reply whose parent is in another matter), and limit the plain not-available requirement to the M-12 (walled) replay.
